Armĭlustrum , i, n.,
I.a place in Rome (in the 13th district), where was celebrated the festival Armilustrium, consecration of arms, ὁπλοκαθαρμός (19th Oct.; v. Inscr. Orell. II. p. 411): “Armilustrum ab ambitu lustri,” Varr. L. L. 5, § 153 Müll.; Liv. 27, 37: “armilustrium ab eo, quod in armilustrio armati sacra faciunt,” Varr. L. L. 6, § 22 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 19 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
